Search Query: I am a pre-school teacher for ages 3-4. Please provide me a detailed report on a strategy for the following situation: One student doesn't want to share and always gets into tantrums when I tell them about the sharing rules. During these tantrums, they hurt other students. They bargain with ice cream, saying they will stop if they get some. I tried to follow a gentle, preventative approach, but it doesn't work for this student.
Evidence nuggets:
- n0 -- Functional behavior assessment to identify triggers and functions -- vital
- n1 -- Observe and collect data before, during, after tantrum -- vital
- n2 -- Form hypothesis on behavior function (e.g., ice‑cream bargaining, control) -- vital
- n3 -- Develop a Positive Behavior Management Plan (PBMP) -- vital
- n4 -- Teach sharing via turn‑taking games and role play -- vital
- n5 -- Model sharing with adult demonstration -- okay
- n6 -- Use visual schedule of sharing sequence -- okay
- n7 -- Provide clear, consistent boundaries -- vital
- n8 -- Offer alternative rewards (stickers, extra playtime) to reinforce sharing -- vital
- n9 -- Use natural and logical consequences (delayed toy access, temporary privilege loss) -- vital
- n10 -- Teach “please ask” language and empathy questions -- vital
- n11 -- Reinforce small sharing attempts with praise -- okay
- n12 -- Implement token system for successful sharing -- vital
- n13 -- Create daily sharing routine to build habit -- vital
- n14 -- Replace ice‑cream distraction with sensory toy or calming activity -- vital
- n15 -- Screen for underlying sensory or language delays -- vital
- n16 -- Collaborate with parents for consistency at home -- vital
- n17 -- Train teacher assistants to cue sharing -- okay
- n18 -- Use calm, low‑tone language when addressing incidents -- vital
- n19 -- Do not give in to ice‑cream bargaining -- vital
- n20 -- Provide distraction early to defuse tantrum -- vital
- n21 -- Use brief time‑out from toy zone if needed -- vital
- n22 -- Document each incident for review -- vital
- n23 -- Adjust plan if behavior persists; consider specialist referral -- vital

Return ONLY the JSON object. Do not use Markdown fences and do not explain.
Research Rubric:
</file>

- n21 -- Use brief time‑out from toy zone if needed -- vital
- n22 -- Document each incident for review -- vital
